criteria.criterion: cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard passes. Tests build records for the trailer, test-suite speedup, prompt-budget and cut A cases and assert which of T1 to T5 fire and before which attempt, matching the section 5.1 table (speedup: T4 fires after the 2nd rejection; cut A: T1 flag with no pause because criteria differ; prompt-budget: T5 flag at 60 minutes).
criteria.evidence: Ran it: all 11 tests passed. The tests trailer_fires_t1_and_t3_before_attempt_3, speedup_t4_pauses_after_second_rejection (T4 is None after the 1st rejection and Pause after the 2nd), cut_a_flags_t1_without_pausing (T1 Flag, T4 None, overall result Flag) and prompt_budget_t5_flags_at_60_minutes (None at 59, Flag at 60 and 80, Pause at 120) each match a row of the section 5.1 table, which I read at docs/design/scope-guard.md lines 128-133.

criteria.criterion: A T4 test fails if the same-criterion comparison is removed or made always-true: a case with two rejections of different criteria must not fire T4 (checkable by reading the test and, if desired, mutating the comparison and running cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard).
criteria.evidence: t4_different_criteria_do_not_pause gives two different criteria and asserts t4_match == No and t4_level == None. If compare_criteria always returned Yes, or always Maybe, t4_match would return that value and the test would fail. The speedup test asserts Pause, so a comparison that always returns No would fail it. I checked this by reading the code; I did not run a mutation because my role does not change files.

criteria.criterion: Line grouping puts a request, its retries and any request that quotes it into one line. T4 normalises criterion text to lower case with numbers removed and returns a maybe result (flag, not pause) on an unclear match. The thresholds in section 5 (T1 3rd attempt, T2 1.5x or 3rd planning round, T3 1.0x/1.5x p90 and $5, T4 two rejections, T5 60/120 minutes) are named constants.
criteria.evidence: group_lines merges a request with the requests named in its retry_of and quotes fields; grouping_joins_retries_and_quoting_requests checks this and passed. normalise_criterion lowercases, strips ASCII digits and collapses whitespace, so 'Under 7 minutes' equals 'under  12 MINUTES'. On an unclear match T4 returns Maybe, which becomes Flag; t4_unclear_match_flags_without_pausing passed. The constants T1_ATTEMPT=3, T2_RATIO=1.5, T2_PLANNING_ROUND=3, T3_FLAG_RATIO=1.0, T3_PAUSE_RATIO=1.5, T3_LINE_DOLLARS=5.0, T4_REJECTIONS=2, T5_FLAG_MINUTES=60 and T5_PAUSE_MINUTES=120 are all present, each documented as an estimate with its basis.

summary: The change does what the request asked, and I found nothing that should block it. The new athena_core::scope_guard module groups a request, its retries and any request that quotes it into one line of work. It computes the five thrash signals T1 to T5 using the section 5 thresholds, each held as a named constant and labelled as an estimate. The module reads no files, runs no processes, makes no network or clock calls, and is exported from lib.rs. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard` and all 11 tests passed. They replay the four named cases and match the section 5.1 table: the speedup case pauses on T4 after the 2nd rejection, cut A gets a T1 flag but no pause, and the prompt-budget case flags T5 at 60 minutes but not at 59. One test gives two rejections with different criteria and checks that T4 does not fire. Reading the code, that test would fail if the same-criterion comparison were removed or made to always match; I did not run that mutation because my role does not change files. D127 is now marked accepted in docs/decisions.md and in scope-guard.md (status line, section 8 and section 13), with both requested changes, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry. All changed files are on the deliverables list. Athena's fmt, clippy and full test runs all passed. My one finding is minor: the new status line in scope-guard.md is longer than the surrounding wrapped lines.
